doc.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Studying bass at Northwestern and Roosevelt University
summary: He chose the string bass over football, studied at Northwestern and graduated from Roosevelt in musical therapy; he studied classically with the bow.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: playing football, but what about your hands? What if something happens to your hands? And eventually he won out. I finally really got serious about the string bass and I studied with a teacher at Northwestern University. I’m from Evanston, Illinois, so I spent a lot of time at Northwestern. And I graduated from Roosevelt University in Chicago in Musical Therapy. But I’ve been working as a musician for years and never really gotten into the musical therapy, but that’s kind of how I got around to the string bass. And once I got into it I had such a rough time, I just decided to stay with it. I never tried to play drums again. And it’s been years of all bass bass.
Let me ask you, you said that your orchestral director was talking about your hands. So did you study classically? You studied with the bow?
You know this is just my observation, I find people that have studied with the bow have incredibly solid intonation.
